core.m1: A seatbelt keeps you safely in your seat.
core.m2: You must wear it during takeoff and landing.
core.e2: The seatbelt sign just turned on.

core.m1: A tray table folds down from the seat in front of you.
core.m2: It is used for meals and drinks.
core.e1: Please put your tray table up.
core.e2: She placed her cup on the tray table.
core.p2: She placed her cup on the _______.

core.m1: A blanket keeps you warm on the plane.
core.m2: Passengers can ask a flight attendant for one.
core.e1: Could I have a blanket, please?
core.e2: He fell asleep under the blanket.

core.m1: A flight attendant takes care of passengers during the flight.
core.m2: They serve food and explain safety rules.
core.e1: The flight attendant brought us water.
core.e2: I asked the flight attendant for a pillow.
core.p2: I asked the _______ for a pillow.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="15" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="11" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: An in-flight meal is food served during the flight.
core.m2: It usually includes a main dish and a drink.
core.e1: The in-flight meal was chicken or pasta.
core.e2: I didn't like the in-flight meal today.

core.m1: A beverage is a drink, such as juice or coffee.
core.m2: Flight attendants offer beverages during the flight.
core.e1: Would you like a beverage before the meal?
core.e2: I chose orange juice as my beverage.
core.p1: Would you like a _______ before the meal?
core.p2: I chose orange juice as my _______.

core.m1: Turbulence is rough, bumpy movement during a flight.
core.m2: Passengers should stay seated when it happens.
core.e1: We felt some turbulence over the ocean.
core.e2: Please sit down, there is turbulence ahead.
core.p1: We felt some _______ over the ocean.
core.p2: Please sit down, there is _______ ahead.

core.m1: Landing is when the plane touches down on the runway.
core.m2: Seatbelts must be fastened before landing.
core.e1: We will begin landing in ten minutes.
core.e2: The landing was smooth and quiet.
core.p1: We will begin _______ in ten minutes.

core.m1: Takeoff is when the plane leaves the ground.
core.m2: Tray tables must be up during takeoff.
core.e2: I always feel nervous during takeoff.

core.m1: Headphones let you listen to music or a movie.
core.m2: Some airlines give them out for free.
core.e1: Could I have some headphones, please?
core.e2: I lost one of my headphones.

core.m1: An aisle is the walking space between rows of seats.
core.m2: Passengers use it to reach the restroom or exit.
core.e1: I prefer an aisle seat, not a window seat.
core.e2: The flight attendant walked down the aisle.
core.p1: I prefer an _______ seat, not a window seat.
core.p2: The flight attendant walked down the _______.

core.m1: The overhead compartment stores bags above your seat.
core.m2: It is closed during takeoff and landing.
core.e1: Could I put my bag in the overhead compartment?
core.e2: The overhead compartment was already full.
core.p1: Could I put my bag in the _______?

core.m1: A safety card explains what to do in an emergency.
core.m2: It is kept in the seat pocket in front of you.
core.e1: Please read the safety card before takeoff.
core.e2: I found the safety card in the seat pocket.
core.p2: I found the _______ in the seat pocket.

core.m1: An emergency exit is a door used to leave the plane quickly if needed.
core.m2: Passengers sitting there may be asked to help in an emergency.
core.e1: The emergency exit is at the back of the plane.
core.e2: She was seated next to the emergency exit.
core.p1: The _______ is at the back of the plane.
core.p2: She was seated next to the _______.

core.m1: A call button lets you ask a flight attendant for help.
core.m2: It is usually located above your seat.
core.e1: I pressed the call button for some water.
core.e2: The call button lit up above seat 12A.
core.p1: I pressed the _______ for some water.

extended.m: Recline means to lean the seat back.
extended.ex: Please recline your seat slowly to avoid bumping others.

extended.m: A window shade blocks sunlight from the window.
extended.ex: Could you please open the window shade?

extended.m: An air vent controls the airflow above your seat.
extended.ex: I turned the air vent to cool down.

extended.m: A reading light is a small light above your seat.
extended.ex: She turned on the reading light to read her book.

extended.m: A seat pocket holds magazines and safety cards.
extended.ex: The menu is in the seat pocket in front of you.

extended.m: A footrest supports your feet during the flight.
extended.ex: He rested his feet on the footrest.

extended.m: A duty-free cart sells tax-free items during the flight.
extended.ex: The duty-free cart is coming down the aisle.

extended.m: A snack is a small amount of food between meals.
extended.ex: Would you like a snack before landing?

extended.m: Coffee is a hot drink served during the flight.
extended.ex: Could I have a cup of coffee?

extended.m: Tea is a hot drink offered as an alternative to coffee.
extended.ex: I'll have tea instead of coffee, thank you.

extended.m: Juice is a cold drink made from fruit.
extended.ex: Orange juice is my favorite in-flight drink.

extended.m: A meal tray holds your in-flight meal and drink.
extended.ex: The flight attendant collected the meal trays after lunch.

extended.m: Cabin pressure is the air pressure inside the plane.
extended.ex: Cabin pressure changes slightly during takeoff and landing.

extended.m: Altitude is the height of the plane above the ground.
extended.ex: We are now cruising at an altitude of 35,000 feet.

extended.m: Cruising means flying steadily at a set altitude.
extended.ex: The plane is now cruising above the clouds.

extended.m: Descend means to go down in altitude.
extended.ex: The plane will descend soon before landing.

extended.m: Ascend means to go up in altitude.
extended.ex: The plane will ascend quickly after takeoff.

extended.m: An announcement is a spoken message over the speaker system.
extended.ex: The captain made an announcement about the weather.

extended.m: In-flight entertainment includes movies, music, and games on your seat screen.
extended.ex: The in-flight entertainment has over 100 movies.

extended.m: A remote control operates the seat-back screen.
extended.ex: The remote control is attached to your armrest.

extended.m: The captain is the pilot in charge of the flight.
extended.ex: The captain welcomed us aboard the flight.

extended.m: The co-pilot assists the captain in flying the plane.
extended.ex: The co-pilot handled the radio communication.

extended.m: The cabin crew are the flight attendants working on the plane.
extended.ex: The cabin crew prepared the cabin for landing.

extended.m: A life vest is safety equipment for water landings.
extended.ex: The life vest is located under your seat.

extended.m: An oxygen mask supplies air in an emergency.
extended.ex: Please put on your own oxygen mask first.

extended.m: A vegetarian meal contains no meat.
extended.ex: I requested a vegetarian meal for this flight.

extended.m: A special meal is a meal that meets a dietary need.
extended.ex: You can order a special meal before your flight.

extended.m: An allergy is a reaction to certain foods or substances.
extended.ex: Please tell us if you have a food allergy.

extended.m: Motion sickness is feeling sick from movement during travel.
extended.ex: She felt motion sickness during the turbulence.

extended.m: Earplugs block out noise so you can rest.
extended.ex: He wore earplugs to sleep on the long flight.

phrases.en: Could I have a blanket, please?
phrases.note: Ask a flight attendant for extra comfort items.
Ask before sitting in an empty seat.
Ask about meal options during service.

phrases.en: Could you please fasten your seatbelt?
phrases.note: A flight attendant's instruction during turbulence or landing.
Tell a flight attendant if you feel unwell.

dialogues.title: Finding Your Seat
dialogues.sit: You board the plane and look for your seat.
lines: It's on the right, near the aisle.
Thank you. Could I put my bag in the overhead compartment?
Of course. Let me help you.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask about seat 15A instead.
dialogues.tn: Practice asking for seat directions politely.

dialogues.title: In-Flight Service
dialogues.sit: The flight attendant offers drinks and meals during the flight.
lines: Would you like something to drink?
Would you like the chicken or the pasta?
I'll have the pasta, thank you.
dialogues.tp: Try again: order tea and choose the vegetarian meal.
dialogues.tn: Practice ordering food and drinks politely.

dialogues.title: Turbulence Problem
dialogues.sit: The plane experiences turbulence during the flight.
lines: Please stay in your seat for now.
Just a few minutes. Thank you for your patience.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask if the flight attendant can bring you water after.
dialogues.tn: Problem scenario: stay calm and follow safety instructions.

dialogues.title: Asking About Landing
dialogues.sit: You want to know when the plane will land.
lines: Excuse me, what time will we land?
We will land in about one hour.
Yes, we are right on schedule.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask about a connecting flight instead.
dialogues.tn: Practice asking for time and schedule information.

dialogues.title: Requesting Headphones
dialogues.sit: You want to watch a movie but don't have headphones.
lines: Excuse me, could I have some headphones?
Thank you. Do you have any snacks?
Yes, we have pretzels and cookies.
Here you go. Enjoy the movie.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask for a blanket instead of headphones.
dialogues.tn: Ask for small items politely using Could I have...?

speaking.q: What do you usually do during a long flight?
speaking.h: I usually watch a movie or listen to music.

speaking.q: Do you prefer the window seat or the aisle seat?
speaking.h: I prefer the window seat because...

speaking.q: What should you do if there is turbulence?
speaking.h: You should fasten your seatbelt and stay in your seat.

speaking.q: What items can you ask a flight attendant for?
speaking.h: You can ask for a blanket, headphones, or a drink.

speaking.q: Describe what happens from takeoff to landing on a flight.
speaking.h: First the plane takes off, then...

culture.title: Being Polite in the Cabin
culture.photo: 📷 An illustrated passenger politely speaking with a flight attendant in the airplane cabin.
culture.notes: Passengers are expected to use polite requests (Could I..., Would you mind...) rather than direct commands when speaking with flight attendants. Staying calm and patient during delays or turbulence is also part of common in-flight etiquette.
qs: What is a polite way to ask for something on a flight?
Why is staying calm during turbulence important?
What should you do if you are unsure about cabin rules?

culture.title: Every Airline Is a Little Different
culture.tz: 每家航空公司規定略有不同
culture.photo: 📷 An illustrated safety card and airline seat pocket showing icons for different rules.
culture.notes: Meal service, baggage rules, and entertainment systems can vary between airlines. Always check the safety card in your seat pocket and listen to announcements instead of assuming every flight works the same way.
qs: Where can you find safety information on a plane?
What are two things that can differ between airlines?
Why is it useful to listen carefully to announcements?

pronunciation.fz: θ 與 ð 的發音

words.tip: Place your tongue lightly between your teeth; don't say a /t/ sound.
Push air out for the voiceless /θ/ before the vowel.
Voice the sound and keep the tongue visible; don't say a /d/.
Feel your throat vibrate for the voiced /ð/.
Keep the /θ/ soft in the middle of the word; don't replace it with /t/.

pronunciation.tip: Chinese speakers often replace /θ/ with /t/ and /ð/ with /d/. Keep the tongue between the teeth for both.
pronunciation.prac: Is there a bathroom near seat thirty? I think so.
